content.title: Hawks vs. Knicks highlights, score: How Atlanta rallied for Game 2 win
content.text: Updated April 20, 2026, 11:54 p.m. ETNEW YORK — The Atlanta Hawks, somehow, stole one in the Garden.The Hawks erased a 12-point deficit at the start of the fourth quarter to stun the New York Knicks 107-106, Monday, April 20 in Game 2 of the first round of the NBA Playoffs.This was a game New York controlled for nearly the majority of the contest. This was a game when Atlanta’s two best players, Jalen Johnson and Nickeil Alexander-Walker, were mostly nonfactors. Yet, veteran guard CJ McCollum, an afterthought in the trade that sent Trae Young to the Washington Wizards, dropped 32 points and six assists in a villainous performance to elevate the Hawks to a 1-1 tie in the series.Jonathan Kuminga, acquired by the Hawks at the trade deadline from the Golden State Warriors, scored 19 points on the bench in a crucial role for Atlanta.The Knicks had the chance to win the game with seconds left, but a Mikal Bridges jumper clanked off the side of the rim.Scroll below for the biggest highlights and analysis from Game 2 of the first-round playoff series between the Atlanta Hawks and New York Knicks: CJ McCollum Game 2 statsMinutes: 35Points: 32Assists: 6Rebounds: 3Steals: 2Block: 1FG: 54.5% (12-for-22)3FG: 30% (3-for-10)FT: 71.4% (5-for-7) Hawks clinging to one-point leadAtlanta scrapped together some defensive possessions and got a massive shot from CJ McCollum to take a lead. Seconds later, Nickeil Alexander-Walker stripped Jalen Brunson and Jalen Johnson took a fastbreak for an easy dunk.The Hawks' four-point lead was short lived, as Jalen Brunson rattled a 3-pointer to close the deficit to one point.The Hawks are up 107-106 with 7.1 seconds left to play. Hawks held (brief) leadAfter OG Anunoby missed a pair of free throws, the Hawks came back to take a three-point lead. Jalen Brunson answered with a 3 to tie the game at 103 with 1:13 left. Atlanta cuts it to oneThe Hawks are making this close, and have cut New York's lead to one point with fewer than three minutes to play. The Hawks have clamped up on defense and have forced the Knicks into tougher shot selection.The Hawks have outscored New York by nine points in the fourth and last held a lead midway through the second quarter.The Knicks are up, 100-99, with 2:43 left to play in the game. Hawks hanging aroundJonathan Kuminga has seen his role increase in Game 2, as Atlanta is hanging around, having shrunk the Knicks lead to just four. Kuminga has 17 points on 6-of-11 shooting.The Knicks are up 96-92, with 6:05 left to play in the game. End Q3: Knicks 91, Hawks 79Tensions are definitely flaring up as we enter the final quarter. The Knicks have taken control of this game, and the Hawks desperately need to both create quick and easy offense and get stops on the other end.Nickeil Alexander-Walker (6 points) and Jalen Johnson (11) continue to struggle, and Atlanta must get more production out of the duo to have any chance for a comeback. CJ McCollum and Jose Alvarado draw double techsAfter Tony Bradley was called for an offensive foul, CJ McCollum and Jose Alvarado each chirped at each other, eventually prompting double technical foul calls by crew chief Zach Zarba. Mitchell Robinson comes in for the KnicksAnd Hawks coach Quin Snyder immediately asks Tony Bradley to step in to counteract Robinson's effectiveness. Jalen Johnson starts to get going, but ...The Knicks have still outscored Atlanta by six just minutes into the second half. One area where the Hawks held an edge over New York in the first half was in 3-point shooting. But Josh Hart and Karl-Anthony Towns each hit a trey just seconds into the third.After missing his first 4 shot attempts in the first half, Hawks All-Star Jalen Johnson connected on a layup and a put-back to get an easy pair. It will be interesting to see if, now, that helps him get going.The Knicks are up 77-64 with 7:27 left to play in the period. A thought on the HawksIt's almost amazing that Atlanta is down just seven points at the half, considering that its two impact players, Jalen Johnson and Nickeil Alexander-Walker, have mostly been non-factors.The pair combined to go 2-for-11 in the first half for 10 combined points. Between the two of them, they only have 4 assists. It's hard to conceive of a way where the Hawks can win if either (or both, really) don't significantly pick it up. End Q2: Knicks 61, Hawks 54It was an engaging and entertaining half, one that has been back-and-forth, with both teams adjusting.The Knicks already have four players in double-figures, with Jalen Brunson leading the way with 12 points. New York is dominating Atlanta in both second-chance points (16-3) and points in the paint (32-16).One of the edges the Hawks have is in 3-point shooting, where Atlanta is 8-of-18 (44.4%).CJ McCollum has been huge for Atlanta, with 18 points on 6-of-9 shooting. Jonathan Kuminga provided excellent minutes off the bench and was a spark on defense, adding 8 points on 3-of-5 shooting. Atlanta All-Star Jalen Johnson's struggles continue; he has recorded just 4 points and still has not made a field goal. Jalen Johnson statsJosh Hart's defense on Jalen Johnson continues to be a deciding factor in this series. Johnson, Atlanta's All-Star point-forward, has had another quiet half. Johnson is 0-for-3 with 4 points, 1 rebound and 0 assists.In the 2025-26 regular season, Johnson averaged 7.9 assists per game.The game is tied at 48, with 2:58 left to play in the half. Make that an 13-2 runThe Hawks are battling back, and have recorded their first lead of the game. It has been defense to launch run, and Hawks coach Quin Snyder has inserted backup center Tony Bradley and backup guard Corey Kispert for the first time in the series.Bradley was signed recently once backup center Jock Landale suffered a sprained ankle. He helps give Atlanta some height and is an answer to New York's Mitchell Robinson.The Hawks are 5-of-8 in the second quarter. Hawks on a 7-0 runAtlanta has leveraged strips and turnovers to launch their fastbreak offense, one element that the Knicks have done a good job of neutralizing.Knicks are still up 33-30, with 9:12 left to play. End Q1: Knicks 32, Hawks 23New York held Atlanta to just 37.5% shooting in the first. After Jalen Brunson dropped 19 points in the first quarter of Game 1 Saturday, he scored just 5 points tonight. Mikal Bridges leads New York with 8 points, while CJ McCollum, once again, has been the most consistent scorer for the Hawks. Tensions flare late in the firstKnicks backup center Mitchell Robinson and Hawks guard Dyson Daniels had some words after Robinson was called for an offensive foul on a screen he set near midcourt. After the play, Robinson walked over Daniels, who got up and quickly chirped back.Both players had to be separated. A replay review determined that Robinson's actions were unsportsmanlike, leading to a technical foul free throw.Nickeil Alexander-Walker drained the free throw. Some more bad news, potentially, for the HawksAtlanta was already undersized in the frontcourt. A lingering injury to Onyeka Okongwu makes Atlanta's depth down low even more precarious. Yet, in the first quarter, Mouhamed Gueye was banged up and had to go into the locker room.That forced Okongwu back on the floor. Sensing a potential advantage, Knicks coach Mike Brown immediately inserted backup center Mitchell Robinson to join Karl-Anthony Towns for a double-big lineup. As good as Josh Hart has been defensively ...A ton of credit has to also go to Mikal Bridges. He has been tasked as the primary defender on Nickeil Alexander-Walker, who had been red hot to end the season. Over the final 15 games of the regular season, Alexander-Walker averaged 24.6 points per game.Bridges has used his length to expertly neutralize Alexander-Walker's effectiveness. Through the first three quarters of Game 1, Alexander-Walker shot just 3-of-12. So far tonight, Alexander-Walker put up just one shot attempt, which he missed, in 6:29 on the floor. Knicks making offense tough for AtlantaCarrying the theme from Game 1, the Knicks are simply making it tough for the Hawks to run through their offense. New York is swarming and collapsing when players try to penetrate, and the Knicks are using active hands to deflect the ball.Early on, the Hawks have one more field goal (3) than they do turnovers (2).The Knicks, meanwhile, are shooting 54.5% from the floor. They're up 15-9 at the first media timeout, with 7:05 left to play in the first. Josh Hart, once again, starts on Jalen JohnsonThe Knicks opened the game with versatile forward Josh Hart guarding Atlanta's best player, Jalen Johnson. It was the matchup New York used last game, to some success. Johnson is a dynamic player who can create his own shot and distribute. But putting Hart on Johnson allows OG Anunoby and Mikal Bridges to guard Atlanta's other two premier wing players.On the first play of the game, Hart harassed Johnson and forced a turnover. Some pre-game observationsI spent some time on the court during pre-game shootaround. Here are some things tha caught my eye:Hawks center Onyeka Okongwu was wearing a big wrap around his right knee during his warmup; he didn't appear to be hindered and was moving around well.Josh Hart went through his regular warm-up but became frustrated when he missed a few consecuitve 3-pointers. He put up several shots and didn't move on until he laced a few.OG Anunoby (left ankle sprain) seemed perfectly fine after he tweaked his ankle Saturday in Game 1. He also didn't appear to be hobbled in any way.Among some of the celebrities who mingled courtside were director Spike Lee, former Knicks center Patrick Ewing, Nebraska Corn Huskers football coach Matt RhuleBoth squads seemed loose, but after talking with some Hawks personnel, they felt Atlanta's players were, understandably, a little eager and nervous ahead of Game 1; many Hawks players were making their playoff debuts then, so it will be interesting to see if the Hawks play a little looser tonight.As always, the crowd here at Madison Square Garden is buzzing. Atlanta Hawks give Onkyeka Okongwu injury updateThe Atlanta Hawks announced that starting center Onyeka Okongwu (right knee inflammation) would be available for tonight’s game.“He’s full go at the outset, and we’ll watch how he’s doing and how he’s feeling,” Hawks coach Quin Snyder told reporters before the game. “How he moves defensively is something that we’re mindful of as well. But like I said, I didn’t think there was any way to keep him out.”“I think for our group, it has been important for me to be urgent with various adjustments,” Snyder added. “Us adapting to things, even if they’re subtle and making decisions that are potentially more impactful, but to be steady for our group. I think some of it for us is focusing on our identity, embracing that.” Hawks vs. Knicks Game 2 oddsOdds courtesy of BetMGM as of 7 p.m. ET on April 20, 2026Spread: Knicks (-6.5)Moneyline: Knicks (-250); Hawks (+200)Over/under: 218.5Knicks vs. Hawks Game 2 injury report*As of Sunday eveningAtlanta HawksJock Landale (right high-ankle sprain): outOnyeka Okonwgu (right knee inflammation): questionableNew York KnicksOG Anunoby (left ankle sprain): probableStream Hawks vs. Knicks Game 2 on PeacockHow to watch Knicks vs. Hawks Game 2Date: Monday, April 20Time: 8 p.m. (ET)Venue: Madison Square GardenLocation: New York, New YorkTV: NBCStreaming: PeacockKnicks vs. Hawks Game 1 recapThe Knicks relied on collective, lockdown defense to smother Atlanta’s role players and bench. On the other end, New York outworked Atlanta on the glass and pushed pace to compromise the Hawks’ transition defense; the Knicks generated a 22-13 edge in fastbreak points.Jalen Brunson led all players with 28 points, though 19 of those came in the first quarter. Karl-Anthony Towns added 25 points and eight rebounds.The Hawks had solid contributions from their four best players – Jalen Johnson, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, CJ McCollum and Onyeka Okongwu – who combined to score 85 points. The rest of Atlanta’s team scored just 17 points.
